one_liner: Intel's assembly-tuned deflate/gzip/zlib codec (igzip): about 4.8x zlib -1 compression speed and 2.3x its decompression speed.
what_it_does: ISA-L is a C library of storage kernels (erasure codes, CRC, RAID parity, zero detection) whose igzip part is a fast compressor and decompressor for the deflate format, with gzip and zlib wrappers. Its API is zlib-like but not zlib's: you fill an isal_zstream or inflate_state struct and call isal_deflate()/isal_inflate() (streaming) or isal_deflate_stateless()/isal_inflate_stateless() (one shot), and levels 1-3 need a caller-supplied level_buf. Output is standard deflate that any inflater reads, and an igzip command-line tool replaces gzip. Since v2.32 an experimental LD_PRELOAD shim (isal-shim.so) intercepts the main zlib deflate/inflate calls plus crc32 and adler32.
how_it_is_fast: The hot loops are hand-written assembly (igzip_body.asm, igzip_deflate_hash.asm, igzip_decode_block_stateless*.asm) for SSE, AVX2 and AVX-512 on x86-64, with aarch64 and riscv64 ports, chosen at runtime by multibinary dispatchers. Compression trades ratio for speed: only four levels (0-3), small hash tables (8K entries at levels 0-1) and greedy matching; level 0 encodes in one pass with a default or user-trained Huffman table, while level 1 and up write an intermediate token stream and then build fully dynamic Huffman codes in a second pass (the '2-pass fully-dynamic' mode of v2.18). Decompression uses two-level Huffman lookup tables (12-bit primary for literal/length, 10-bit for distance) so most symbols decode in one table lookup.
when_to_use: High-throughput gzip/zlib production where output must stay deflate-compatible: storage, log shipping, HTTP responses, container image layers (containerd can call igzip -cd, per issue #255).
Fast compression at ratios near zlib -1: in the TurboBench run igzip -1 reached 615 MB/s at 36.9% against zlib -1 at 127 MB/s and 36.5%.
Decompressing gzip/deflate faster than zlib (about 970-1080 MB/s vs 449-484 MB/s for zlib in the same run) when you cannot switch formats.
x86-64 servers, especially with AVX2 or AVX-512, where Intel tuned the assembly; aarch64 and riscv64 have their own kernels.
Projects that also need ISA-L's CRC, erasure-code or RAID kernels and want a single dependency.
when_not_to_use: Archival or bandwidth-bound use where ratio matters: igzip's best level (3, 35.5%) is worse than zlib -6/-9 (zlib -9 31.9%) and libdeflate (-6 31.9%, -12 30.5%) in the same table.
Decompression only: libdeflate decoded slightly faster (1075-1134 MB/s) than igzip in the same run, and has a simpler build.
Builds without NASM 2.14.01+ (x86-64) or on 32-bit x86, which v2.32 dropped; other architectures fall back to portable C base functions without the speedup.

Code that needs an exact zlib API or behaviour: the shim is marked experimental, Linux-only, intercepts a subset of functions and skips custom zlib headers and automatic gzip header detection; SYNC_FLUSH/FULL_FLUSH always emit a sync marker, unlike zlib.
Untrusted inputs where you want a hardened API: the README says parameters are not fully validated (NULL or invalid inputs are undefined behaviour).

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (autotools, Makefile.unx, nmake on Windows; CMake experimental and only verified on x86_64)
integration.dependencies: none at runtime; NASM 2.14.01+ to build on x86-64, gas 2.24+ and GCC 10.1+ on aarch64, gas 2.39+ and GCC 12.1+ for RISC-V vector
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler (gcc, clang, icc or MSVC) plus an assembler as above; C API with extern "C" guards
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE through AVX-512, runtime dispatch), aarch64, riscv64 (RVV); Linux, Windows, macOS, FreeBSD; portable C base functions elsewhere; 32-bit x86 removed in v2.32
integration.thread_safety: not documented in the README; all compression and decompression state lives in caller-owned isal_zstream / inflate_state structs (plus level_buf), so one stream per thread is the natural pattern; issue #249 (July 2023) asked for thread-safety documentation
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — deflate/gzip/zlib output is compatible, but the native API differs from zlib; the experimental isal-shim.so LD_PRELOAD layer covers deflateInit/deflate/inflate and related calls, crc32 and adler32, falling back to system zlib for the rest

gotchas: Levels 1-3 fail with ISAL_INVALID_LEVEL_BUF unless you allocate level_buf yourself (suggested sizes ISAL_DEF_LVLx_DEFAULT); only levels 0-3 exist, so zlib levels 4-9 have no equivalent.

v2.32.1 fixed several memory-safety bugs (integer-overflow out-of-bounds write in isal_write_gzip_header, use-after-free in generate_custom_hufftables, an internal buffer overrun in igzip, zlib DICTID byte order); stay on 2.32.1 or later.

Open issue #405 (April 2026) reports that isal_inflate_stateless() can leave its loop early and skip the CRC check on a successful decode; check return codes and verify checksums yourself if this matters.
Compile-time options IGZIP_HIST_SIZE (window, default 32K) and LONGER_HUFFTABLE change struct layouts, so the library and its users must be built with the same settings.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick igzip over zlib-ng or libdeflate when you need the fastest deflate-compatible compression at low levels (in the TurboBench run, igzip -1 at 615 MB/s vs libdeflate -3 at 185 MB/s) and can accept a lower ratio; pick libdeflate for best deflate ratio or one-shot decompression, zlib-ng for a mature zlib-API drop-in, and LZ4 or zstd if you are free to leave the deflate format.
verified_claims_summary: An independent TurboBench run by its author in zlib-ng issue 1486 (May 2023, silesia.tar, AMD Ryzen 6600HS laptop, compiler not stated) measured igzip level 1 compressing at 615 MB/s with 36.9% ratio vs zlib level 1 at 127 MB/s with 36.5% (4.8x, derived from page data), and igzip decompressing at 969-1081 MB/s vs zlib's 449-484 MB/s (about 2.3x).
status_note: Actively maintained by Intel (last commit 2026-09-30, release v2.32.1), BSD-3-Clause and packaged by distros and conda-forge, so it is easy to adopt as a system library, though building from source needs NASM on x86-64.
